prompt.context: Our client is Vidi-Games, a manufacturer and retailer of video games. They are planning to enter the Brazilian market. One of the factors that has prevented them from entering that market is that there is a tariff for importing products that can be produced in the country of 50% of production costs. However, the government is planning to lower it down to 15% in the next years, decreasing it 5% every year (from 50% to 45%, and so on).
prompt.question: What variables should they consider? What is the market size? Should they enter the market? And if so, should they export the product from China to Brazil or produce it in Brazil?

clarifying_info.q: What is the retail price per video game?
What is the production cost in China?
What are the production costs in Brazil?
What are the other cost components?
clarifying_info.a: Distribution $6, Labor $8, Overhead $6, Other costs $10.4 — these apply in both scenarios.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of Brazil?
What share of the population is under 35?
What share of the population is considered poor (cannot afford the product)?
What is the average household size?
What is the penetration rate of video games among the affluent and young segment?
How many games does an average household buy per year?
What is the required investment to enter Brazil?

framework: Market entry viability: industry analysis, competitive landscape, regulatory environment (tariffs, repatriation, currency, inflation, culture)
Market sizing: estimate total addressable market in Brazil (population segmentation approach)
Profitability analysis: revenue minus costs under two production scenarios (China export vs. local Brazil production)
Break-even and tariff sensitivity: at what tariff rate does the venture become profitable?
Investment payback: how long to recover the $100M entry investment as tariff steps down?
Strategic alternatives: options if the company needs to enter sooner than the tariff schedule allows

questions.prompt: Estimate the total number of video games expected to be sold in Brazil per year.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment Brazil's population by age (under 35 = gaming demographic), affordability (affluent 40%), household size, penetration rate, and games per household. All figures should be provided after the candidate attempts an estimate.

math.setup: Total video games = [(Population x % young x % affluent) / avg household size] x penetration rate x games per household per year

questions.prompt: Under the current 50% tariff, is it profitable to enter Brazil — and does it matter whether production is in China or Brazil?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total costs per unit for each scenario and compare to $50 price. Key insight: at 50% tariff, the China production cost grossed up equals Brazil production cost, so both yield identical (negative) profit.

math.setup: Revenue per unit = $50. Fixed cost components: Distribution $6 + Labor $8 + Overhead $6 + Other $10.4 = $30.4
math.answer: Loss of $1.40 per unit; both scenarios are equally unprofitable under the 50% tariff. Company should NOT enter now.

questions.prompt: At what tariff rate does Vidi-Games break even? When will that tariff be reached given the 5%-per-year reduction schedule?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set Revenue = Costs and solve for the break-even tariff X. Then map that rate to the government's step-down schedule.

steps: At 35% tariff (3 years from now): cost = $14 x 1.35 + $30.4 = $18.9 + $30.4 = $49.3; profit = $50 - $49.3 = $0.70 per unit
Break-even is reached at 40% (year 2); entry makes sense beginning year 3 at 35% tariff
math.answer: Break-even tariff is 40%, reached in 2 years. The company can profitably enter in year 3 at a 35% tariff, earning $0.70/unit and $15.75M total profit in year 3.

questions.prompt: What is the annual profit once the tariff reaches its minimum of 15%? How long will it take to recoup the $100M investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate calculates profit at 15% tariff, then builds a simple payback schedule year by year. The tariff steps down 5%/yr, so profits grow each year. Exact payback can be calculated to days.

math.answer: Full investment recovered in approximately 3 investment-years + 31 days (i.e., ~5 years from today, or 3 years after entry in year 3). A good answer is 'just over 3 years after entry.'

brainstorming.prompt: What could Vidi-Games do if they needed to enter the Brazilian market now, before the tariff comes down?

categories.name: Revenue side
ideas: Analyze viability of a price increase above $50
Note: increasing volume alone does not help when profit per unit is negative

categories.name: Cost side
ideas: Move manufacturing to lower-cost locations within or outside Brazil
Optimize distribution network to reduce the $6 distribution cost
If producing in Brazil, investigate ways to reduce the $21 production cost

categories.name: Strategic / structural options
ideas: Enter into a partnership with a Brazilian partner to share costs or gain local advantages
Acquire an existing competitor in Brazil
Sell to retailers at wholesale (avoiding distribution, labor, overhead) at a reduced price — trading margin for lower cost base

recommendation: Do not enter Brazil under the current 50% tariff — the business is unprofitable at -$1.40 per unit regardless of whether production is in China or Brazil
Enter the Brazilian market in year 3 when the tariff reaches 35%, at which point the venture earns $0.70/unit and $15.75M annually
Scale up as the tariff continues to decline to 15%, at which point annual profit reaches $78.75M
The $100M investment is fully recovered approximately 3 years after entry (just over 5 years from today)
risks: Tariff reduction could be delayed or reversed by the Brazilian government
Market size assumptions (penetration, household size, income distribution) carry uncertainty
Currency risk and repatriation costs could erode profitability
Competitors may enter earlier, eroding Vidi-Games' market share
next_steps: Monitor the Brazilian tariff legislation annually
Identify a local Brazilian partner or acquisition target now to be ready for year-3 entry
Develop a phased market entry plan (pilot in a major city, then scale)
Explore cost reduction levers in production and distribution to improve per-unit economics
